title: Nodal recognition from local complete intersection fibres and an unramified singular subscheme
statement: Let $g:T\to B$ be a flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], locally finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. For every algebraically closed field $\Omega$ and geometric point $y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to B$ [def-weil-geometric-point], suppose the geometric fibre $C_y=T\times_B\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-geometric-fibre] is empty or pure of dimension $1$ [def-weil-pure-dimension] and a local complete intersection over $\Omega$. Here local complete intersection over $\Omega$ means admitting an affine open cover by spectra of finitely generated $\Omega$-algebras which are local complete intersections as defined in [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]. Let $Z=\operatorname{Sing}(g)\hookrightarrow T$ be the closed subscheme cut out by the first Fitting ideal of relative differentials [def-trf-first-fitting-singular-subscheme]. If $Z\to B$ is unramified [def-weil-unramified-morphism], then for every such $\Omega,y$, every point $z\in C_y$ at which $C_y\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is not smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] is closed in $C_y$ [def-weil-closed-points] and its maximal-ideal-adic completed local ring [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] is isomorphic to $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. The empty fibres impose no condition.

proof.text: Fix $\Omega,y$ and write $C=T\times_B\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. If $C$ is empty there is nothing to prove. Otherwise $C$ is pure of dimension $1$ and has the stipulated affine lci cover. Each chart algebra is finitely generated over $\Omega$, so $C$ is locally of finite type. Also $g$ is locally of finite type: its finite-presentation charts have finitely many algebra generators.

source.place: Tag 0C59 (lemma-nodal-family), reduction to a geometric fibre; finite-generation unpacking.

proof.text: Let $p:C\to T$. Relative differential base change identifies $p^*\Omega^1_{T/B}$ with $\Omega^1_{C/\Omega}$ and supplies finite-type quasi-coherence. Isomorphic finite-type modules have the same Fitting ideals (transport a generating surjection and its kernel along the isomorphism), and the Fitting pullback theorem says its ideal $\operatorname{Fit}_1$ is, on affines, the minor ideal used in the definition of the first-Fitting singular subscheme. The Fitting pullback theorem therefore identifies the first-Fitting closed subscheme $W=\operatorname{Sing}(C/\Omega)$ with $C\times_T Z$. The fibre-product universal property identifies this with $Z\times_B\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$: both parameterize maps to $Z$ and $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ agreeing over $B$. Thus $W\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is unramified by base change.

By the field-curve Fitting/smooth preparation, the nonsmooth points of $C/\Omega$ are exactly $|W|$. Since unramifiedness includes local finite type, the unramified-over-field local criterion applies to $W$ and says every point of $W$ is closed in $W$.

source.place: Tag 0C4E (lemma-nodal-lci), (2) implies (1); Divisors Tag 0C3K and Morphisms Tag 02G7.

proof.text: Let $z$ be any nonsmooth point of $C$. Its corresponding singleton is closed in $W$ by step 3. The inclusion $W\hookrightarrow C$ identifies $W$ homeomorphically with a closed subset of $C$. Hence $\{z\}$ is closed in that closed subset, and therefore in $C$. This proves the required closedness for every nonsmooth point, not just for points initially assumed closed.

Apply (2) implies (1) of the nodal-curve lci criterion to $C/\Omega$: local finite type and pure dimension $1$ hold by step 1, the lci cover is a hypothesis, and its first-Fitting subscheme is unramified by step 2. Thus every closed point is smooth or a node. The point $z$ of step 4 is closed and nonsmooth, hence a node. Let $\iota:\Omega\to\bar\Omega$ be the algebraic closure used in the node condition. Every element of $\bar\Omega$ is algebraic over $\iota(\Omega)$, and $\iota(\Omega)$ is algebraically closed, so it lies in $\iota(\Omega)$: $\iota$ is an isomorphism of fields (for instance $\iota=\operatorname{id}$). Hence $\operatorname{Spec}\bar\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is an isomorphism, and by the fibre-product universal property so is the projection $q:C_{\bar\Omega}\to C$; the only point $\bar z$ over $z$ is $q^{-1}(z)$, and $q$ induces an isomorphism $\mathcal O_{C,z}\cong\mathcal O_{C_{\bar\Omega},\bar z}$ of local rings, hence of their maximal-ideal-adic completions. Composing with $\bar\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)\cong\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ induced by $\iota^{-1}$ on coefficients, the criterion's node condition gives precisely $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{C,z}\simeq\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$. Since $\Omega,y,z$ were arbitrary this proves the assertion.
